title: fix(spec,objectql): name the aggregated column at `having`, PostgreSQL only at `where`
body:
Fixes #20510

Clause-②: no

## What changed

Two false phrases in the number-comparand refusal, at two positions:

1. **`having` said "a declared number field".** The column at `having`
   (`total`, an aggregation alias or a groupBy projection) has no declared
   `FieldType` of its own — the door hands the verdict a synthesized
   `{ type: 'number' }` for whatever the engine classes numeric
   (`aggregatedRowColumnClasses`). It now says "a numeric aggregated column".
2. **The `not-a-number` / `boolean` / `date` clauses named PostgreSQL's server
   error at every position.** Only `where` (both spellings) ever reaches a
   live driver bind; `having` and the per-aggregation `filter` are evaluated
   by the engine itself, in JS, before any row is read, on every driver
   alike — no driver ever sees the comparand there. The clause now appears
   only where the driver actually binds it.

**Measured, and the card's own claim corrected:** the per-aggregation
`filter`'s column is a real declared field, not an aggregated one — that
position narrows the object's RAW source rows *before* aggregation runs,
against the object's declared field map (confirmed by both the door's own
header and the existing pin at `aggregations[1].filter.f_number.$gt`, which
already reads `'f_number' compares a declared number field`). So only its
PostgreSQL clause moves; its "declared … field" wording is unchanged.

### Before / after

| position | column | before | after |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `where` | declared field | `… compares a declared number field against "abc" …, which is not a number: it has no numeric reading, and backends answer it differently (PostgreSQL with a server error).` | unchanged, byte for byte |
| per-aggregation `filter` | declared field | `… compares a declared number field against "abc" …: it has no numeric reading, and backends answer it differently (PostgreSQL with a server error).` | `… compares a declared number field against "abc" …: it has no numeric reading.` |
| `having` | aggregated column | `… compares a declared number field against "abc" at having.total.$gt, which is not a number: it has no numeric reading, and backends answer it differently (PostgreSQL with a server error).` | `… compares a numeric aggregated column against "abc" at having.total.$gt, which is not a number: it has no numeric reading.` |

The accept set is unchanged — no refusal added or removed, words only.

### Mechanism

`NumberComparandRefusalSite` (`@objectstack/spec`) gains two optional fields,
both defaulting to the pre-existing `where` behaviour so an existing site (or
one built before this change) renders identically:

- `aggregated?: boolean` — the column is an aggregated-row column, not a
  declared field. Only `having` sets it.
- `boundByDriver?: boolean` — this position reaches a live driver bind. Only
  `where` sets it `true`; default is `true` for backward compatibility.

The engine door (`@objectstack/objectql`) passes both at its three call
sites — it already knew which position it was building a refusal for; no
second rule, and no driver-level change.

## Acceptance notes

- Out of scope, noted only: a `{ $field }`-adjacent structural filter shape
  (`where { amount: { "a": 1 } }`) was already flagged by PR #20545's at-tier
  review as a class (a) finding for the filing seat to pick up; this PR does
  not touch it.
- `packages/rest`'s `data-number-comparand-door.test.ts` asserts no phrase at
  `having` / the per-aggregation `filter` (only status/path), and its `where`
  phrase pin is unaffected — left untouched, per the claimed file surface.

## Tests (all green, fresh builds)

- `@objectstack/spec` build, then `vitest run filter-number-comparand-declared-type.test.ts`
  — **47/47 passed**, including new cases for `aggregated` / `boundByDriver`
  and a byte-for-byte pin that the pre-existing `where` message is unchanged;
  `pnpm typecheck` — clean (no new errors).
- `@objectstack/objectql` build, then `vitest run engine-number-comparand-declared-type-door.test.ts
  engine-aggregate-having-temporal-door.test.ts` — **85/85 passed**; `pnpm typecheck` — clean.
- `@objectstack/rest` build, then `vitest run data-number-comparand-door.test.ts`
  — **4 passed, 8 skipped** (PostgreSQL/MySQL cells skipped as before; no code
  change was needed there).
- `check:api-surface`, `check:dual-source-exports`, `check:entry-nameability`,
  `check:exported-any`, `check:lean-entry-closure` — all green against the
  fresh build (the widened `NumberComparandRefusalSite` type doesn't move the
  name-level api-surface snapshot).
- Derived gate sweep (`dispatch-gates.mjs`, 86 commands): all green except 3
  that need the WHOLE workspace built (`check:doc-formula-expressions`,
  `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:type-check-debt --re-measure`) — out
  of this diff's local scope, left to CI.

Full command list and exit codes are in the report comment on the issue.
